title: Hybrid dynamical decoupling and coherent driving for high-fidelity nuclear-spin control in diamond
authors: Jiwon Jeon, Donghun Jung, Eunsang Lee, Junghyun Lee
abstract: Nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond provide room-temperature electron-nuclear spin registers for quantum sensing and quantum information processing, with surrounding 13C nuclear spins serving as long-lived quantum memories. However, coherent control of large nuclear-spin registers is limited by finite electron-spin coherence and spectral addressability. Existing approaches follow two complementary strategies: dynamical-decoupling (DD) gates exploit filter-function resonances to realize selective conditional evolution but permit only discrete rotation angles, whereas dynamical-decoupling radio-frequency (DDrf) control restores continuous tunability at the cost of stringent hyperfine-geometry and RF-power requirements. Here, we introduce hybrid dynamical-decoupling and radio-frequency (H-DDrf) control, which preserves the DD-induced conditional evolution and employs a geometrically phase-matched RF drive to complete the target operation. This approach reduces both RF power and gate duration while maintaining high-fidelity control, thereby expanding the accessible 13C nuclear-spin register for room-temperature NV-based quantum memories and quantum processors.
summary: This paper introduces a novel Hybrid Dynamical-Decoupling and Radio-Frequency (H-DDrf) control technique for manipulating nuclear spins in diamond NV centers. By intelligently combining the selectivity of DD with the continuous tunability of RF driving, the method enhances quantum control fidelity. This advancement expands the usable quantum memory capacity for room-temperature quantum processors.
main_problem: The primary challenge is achieving high-fidelity, continuous quantum control over large registers of nuclear spins coupled to NV centers in diamond at room temperature.
main_result: The proposed Hybrid Dynamical-Decoupling and Radio-Frequency (H-DDrf) control scheme successfully maintains high fidelity while reducing required RF power and gate duration compared to existing methods.
method: The authors combine the frequency-selective conditional evolution provided by Dynamical Decoupling (DD) with a geometrically phase-matched RF drive to complete the target rotation, achieving continuous tunability.
model_or_system: The system utilizes Nitrogen-Vacancy (NV) centers in diamond, employing surrounding $^{13}	ext{C}$ nuclear spins as long-lived quantum memories. The control relies on understanding the hyperfine coupling Hamiltonian ($\hat{H}_0$) and its geometric dependencies.
key_observables: Conditional-operation contrast ($\mathcal{F}_{	ext{CR}}$) and coherence-weighted fidelity ($\mathcal{F}_{	ext{CR}}^{w_c}$), measured as functions of RF frequency and initial RF phase.
important_parameters: Hyperfine geometry parameters ($	heta_A,  eta_A$), RF Rabi frequency ($\Omega_{	ext{RF}}$), and the required phase matching condition ($\varphi_0 = 	heta_A - \delta\varphi$).
main_assumptions: The DD sequence establishes a frequency-selective baseline, and the RF drive acts as a resonant correction to complete the operation, rather than replacing the DD dynamics entirely.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the H-DDrf protocol, compare controllability/tunability against DD-only and DDrf, and show fidelity measurements ($\mathcal{F}_{	ext{CR}}$) across different RF parameters and hyperfine geometries.
paper_structure: The paper first reviews the limitations of existing DD and DDrf methods, then introduces the H-DDrf protocol, derives the necessary phase-matching conditions, and finally presents detailed comparisons of fidelity and robustness against various experimental imperfections.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the practical limitations of scaling quantum memories by providing a robust, high-fidelity control mechanism for multi-spin systems, which is central to quantum computation.
